notes:
POC focused on Dedicated capacity throughput and latency SLOs for live telemetry use cases. Customer requires predictable tail latency for 1k-2k RPS of short inference calls (avg prompt ~120 tokens, response ~80 tokens) for operator-assist and alert enrichment. They run heavy embedding pipelines for anomaly search (batch embedding windows of 10k items hourly).

Key quantitative targets called out by customer: p95 <= 150ms for single-turn chat (tokenized request length 200), p99 <= 350ms; sustained throughput 800-1200 requests/sec with burst to 2k for 30s without SLA degradation. Cost sensitivity moderate — want to understand cost per 1M tokens on dedicated pool vs hosted.

Customer infrastructure constraints: must sit inside their VPC for ingest and have private egress to their data lake; EU data residency for subset of telemetry. KMS integration required for key management. SOC2 cert already in place; legal pushing for an uptime SLA and credits tied to latency SLO misses.

Notes from last call (2026-02-25): "We need a 48h soak that mirrors prod traffic patterns — spikes every 10 minutes, lots of short infercalls and periodic large embedding batches." They asked for a kernel-level explanation of how Redwood handles KV cache warmup during soak. SE promised kernel selection notes + sample load config.

Customer quote: "If we can hit p95 at scale with consistent cost math, we can commit to reserved monthly capacity for Q3."
poc_summary: Agreement to run staged POC on Dedicated: 1) baseline single-node latency tests (cold/warm cache); 2) scaled load runs to determine GPUs required for target throughput (start 2xA100 equiv, scale to 8x); 3) 48h soak with production traffic replay (spikes & background embedding jobs); 4) compare cost-per-token vs hosted; 5) negotiate SLA language (latency SLOs, credit matrix, capacity burst). SE to provide load scripts and representative prompt set. Legal to review SLA draft post-soak.
